messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV-cache continuous-batching spike detected in prod cluster 'infer-eu-3'. Latency > SLO for 3m, error-rate ↑, affected models: llm-llama-v3, mistral-xl-gqa, qwen-mqa-1. Alert id: #INC-3180001
aj: I'm on it. grabbing recent graphs. linking dashboard: https://console.redwood/s/grafana/d/kv-cache-spike
maya: noticed a sharp rise in KV size and continuous-batch queue depth ~10:23 UTC. Looks like a pattern of many unique prefixes from a customer test workload.
liam: can you dump slowlog or head of the eviction trace?
aj: running `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/kv-cache-frontend --since=15m | head -n 200` now
aj: paste: ```
Evict loop: shard=72 evict_count=23456 kv_bytes=1.9GB prefix_cardinality=8.4M contbatch_windows=120 active_batches=420
WARN: batch-window exceeded 350ms on shard=72
```
maya: that prefix_cardinality looks wrong for normal traffic. probably a burst of high-cardinality prompts.
product-ops: any customer impacted? need to surface to CS if this hits paid SLAs.
customer-success: I'm triaging customer telemetry. Two enterprise customers (acct: white-fox / acct: blue-lake) show latency spikes and 504s. Preparing a customer note.
aj: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce cont-batch window from 50ms -> 20ms 2) enable per-model cache-size caps for llm-llama-v3 and qwen-mqa-1 3) fallback policy to smaller quantized variant for new sessions.
liam: reducing window will increase PU but should lower in-flight KV growth. want me to push a hot-config?
maya: yes do a canary first on shard group infer-eu-3a. use `rbac` canary rollout.
aj: prepping patch: ```yaml
# /configs/contbatch-hotfix.yaml
contbatch:
  default_window_ms: 20
  per_model_overrides:
    llm-llama-v3:
      cache_size_mb: 512
      ttl_s: 120
    qwen-mqa-1:
      cache_size_mb: 768
      ttl_s: 90
  circuit_breaker:
    enabled: true
    max_inflight_batches: 200
```
aj: deploying canary to eu-3a now: `rdwctl deploy config contbatch-hotfix --target infer-eu-3a --canary`
sre-bot: Deploy started by aj for contbatch-hotfix -> infer-eu-3a (canary). CI: green. Rolling 2 pods.
liam: canary pods up. monitoring error budget and KV-size on canary shards.
maya: initial telemetry: canary shows tail latency drop ~30% and active_batches halved on canary shards. Nice.
aj: rolling to eu-3b after 5m stable.
product-ops: flagging to set incident severity to Sev2 given customer 504s.
customer-success: sent initial customer note: "we're investigating a performance regression affecting KV cache; temporary mitigation underway; will update in 30m".
liam: noticed Mistral GQA model has very different access pattern - GQA requests create many small keys (question-specific) causing eviction thrash. Need separate per-model heuristics.
nina: can we add a quick heuristic: if prefix_cardinality increase > 1M in 1m, switch model to per-request bypass cache?
maya: good call. that would prevent cache thrash for models with high key churn. Anyone can code the flip?
aj: I'll add a toggle behind feature-flag: `contbatch.bypass_on_cardinality_spike` and enable for mistral-xl-gqa on eu. Patch in progress.
aj: applied global rollout to all eu shards. watching.
liam: graph: https://console.redwood/s/graphs/kv-size?range=30m shows global KV size peaking then trending down after canary.
customer-success: white-fox reports degraded but usable, blue-lake still seeing 20% elevated latencies. Sending follow-up.
maya: I still see elevated memory on llm-llama-v3 nodes. suspect long-lived sessions holding huge KV entries (Llama returns large hidden states). Propose evict-on-reset for sessions older than 5m.
liam: agree. That's safer than global TTL. Add session-based TTL: `session_ttl_s: 300` default.
aj: rolling session-ttl change with canary. Keeping circuit-breaker active.
product-ops: capture a short postmortem page after we stabilize. Need customer impact timeline and root cause hypothesis.
nina: root cause hypothesis draft: "a background synthetic test from an enterprise customer generated unprecedented prefix diversity; combined with a recent cont-batch window increase from 20->100ms in last week, allowed continuous batches to accumulate, inflating KV cache and triggering eviction thrash, impacting models with high per-request variability (Mistral-GQA) and long-lived KV consumers (Llama). Qwen-MQA suffered due to mismatch in prefetch heuristic causing duplicate keys."
maya: agree. also note we had no per-model circuit-breaker previously. adding it prevented full cascade.
aj: current status: reduced contbatch window and per-model caps deployed globally in EU; circuit-breaker enabled; session-ttl applied to llama nodes; mistral set to bypass cache on cardinality spike. Metrics improving: P95 latency down to near baseline, error-rate dropping.
liam: infra step: recommend increasing shard headroom on eu-3 by 10% to handle remaining tail while we tune heuristics.
maya: booking follow-up meeting with ML infra and model owners to land permanent heuristics: per-model cache policies, prefetch safeguards, and adjust contbatch algorithm to consider prefix entropy.
product-ops: creating incident doc: https://console.redwood/s/incidents/INC-3180001 with timeline and actions. Assigning postmortem owners: maya, aj, liam.
customer-success: final customer update sent: "mitigations applied; we saw significant improvement; internal follow-up will refine settings; will share postmortem".
aj: switching to monitoring-only mode. if no regressions in next 1h I'll mark incident resolved and do formal postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident INC-3180001 updated to status: mitigation_applied.
maya: handing off to overnight oncall @liam for monitoring; I'm OOO after 22:15 UTC. liam please escalate if we see >10% error-rate for >10m.
liam: got it. oncall takeover acknowledged. :white_check_mark:
customer-success: will keep customers updated. closing customer loop once postmortem is ready.
sre-bot: Note: created an automated alert to detect prefix_cardinality > 500k sustained for 2m and auto-toggle bypass for configured models.
aj: great. thanks everyone. final note: we should add a small chaos test to simulate high-prefix-cardinality to avoid regressions in future.
maya: agreed. PR for chaos test in repo infra-tests/chaos/prefix-cardinality coming this week. :rocket:
